reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be any complete real inner-product space with its normed additive commutative group structure, and let f:E→ℝ be continuously Fréchet differentiable on all of E. Let α, β, R, ε be strictly positive real numbers. Assume f is α-strongly convex on E with the normalization f((1−t)x+ty) ≤ (1−t)f(x)+tf(y)−(α/2)t(1−t)‖x−y‖² for every x,y∈E and t∈[0,1]. For every z,x₀∈E such that f(z)≤f(x) for all x∈E and ‖x₀−z‖≤R, consider any map A:E×ℝ×ℝ→E×ℕ and any map φ:ℝ→ℕ. Suppose that for every y∈E and every real r,δ, if r>0, δ>0, and ‖y−z‖≤r, then, writing A(y,r,δ)=(v,c), both f(v)−f(z)≤δ and c≤φ(βr²/δ) hold. The same fixed minimizer z is used in every such call guarantee. No condition on A for other inputs, no smoothness bound involving β, and no monotonicity assumption on φ is asserted.

Define L=ln(αR²/ε)/ln(4), N=⌈L⌉₊∈ℕ (the natural-number ceiling, equal to zero for L≤0 and otherwise the least natural number at least L), and r_k=R/2^k for every k∈ℕ. Define a state-and-cost sequence (x_k,c_k) by (x_0,c_0)=(x₀,0), and for each k∈ℕ define (v_k,d_k)=A(x_k,r_k,αr_k²/8) and (x_{k+1},c_{k+1})=(v_k,c_k+d_k). After these N recursive calls, define (x_*,d_*)=A(x_N,√(ε/α),ε) and the natural-number total cost C=c_N+d_*. The square root is the nonnegative real square root; its argument here is positive.

Then all of the following conclusions hold simultaneously: (1) N≤max{0,L}+1, interpreting N as a real number; (2) N=0 if and only if αR²≤ε; (3) ‖x_N−z‖≤r_N; (4) f(x_*)−f(z)≤ε; (5) C≤N·φ(8(β/α))+φ(β/α), an inequality in ℕ; and (6) C≤(max{0,L}+1)·φ(8(β/α))+φ(β/α), an inequality in ℝ with C and the values of φ coerced to real numbers. In addition, the single extra hypothesis φ(β/α)≤φ(8(β/α)) implies the conjunction of both (7) C≤(max{0,L}+2)·φ(8(β/α)) and (8) if 4≤αR²/ε, then C≤3L·φ(8(β/α)); these latter bounds are real inequalities. Thus the bound in (8) is nested under both the comparison of the two φ values and the ratio condition 4≤αR²/ε; the ratio condition alone is not stated to imply that bound.

When αR²≤ε, N=0 and the recursion contributes the initial pair (x₀,0); the final call A(x₀,√(ε/α),ε) is still made and contributes its cost. In this case the natural-number bound (5) reduces to C≤φ(β/α). Equality αR²=ε is included in this zero-recursion case. Costs and φ values may themselves be zero: they are only required to be natural numbers, and the stated inequalities remain valid without any positivity assumption on them.
